source_quality.notes: The text layer is not valid UTF-8 and every displayed formula is corrupted in it, so equations (1) to (17) and Figures 6, 7, 8 and 10 were read from review proxies. Render pages are 1191 by 1684 pixels at 144 dpi, and printed footer page N sits two render pages behind the printed number. The prose is non-native and typo-dense; its slips are preserved rather than corrected.

task_reconstruction.summary: Measure the maturity of a cargo firm's data-and-analytics system, raise it under a budget, mine a protocol from simulated scores, and test whether the same model serves ports of different size.

section_map.summary: The summary builds the model and reports the four tasks: the score 0.8173, the simulation check, the association rules, and the size test.
Section 1 turns cold data into the motive, traces the maturity model to its 1979 prototype, and hands the plan to a figure.
Section 2 states four assumptions, each with a justification.
Section 3 hands every symbol to one table.
Section 4 selects seventeen indicators by grounded theory and weights them by entropy mixed with a judgement matrix.
Section 5 converts the goal into a linear program and checks a system-dynamics simulation by its percentage error.
Section 6 discretizes the simulated scores and mines association rules.
Section 7 reweights by seaport size and argues the model transfers.
Section 8 lists strengths and concedes two limits.
A letter to seaport users is printed after the reference list.

contributions.summary: Seventeen indicators split into people, technology and process, selected by grounded theory under three stated principles.
A blend of entropy weights and hierarchy weights whose two shares are fixed by matching distances.
A linear program that maximizes the improved score under a unit cap and a budget.
An association-rule protocol that names the level each component must reach.

dependency_graph.via: the blended weights scale the indicator scores
the current scores and weights fix the objective
they are the reference series the simulation is measured against

assumptions.summary: The system covers people, technology and process; any indicator found later counts as maturity still to be improved.
The literature checked is comprehensive and scientific, justified only by restating the assumption.
Customers are firms; self-employed individuals are ignored as being of little value.
The cost of improving each indicator is known, justified only by the purpose of the analysis.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Indicator scores are normalized by their column sum before the entropy is computed.
Simulated scores are cut into five maturity bands and four bands each for people and technology.

models.summary: A scoring model that lifts a base score by a tenth per concern and rescales the weighted sum.
An entropy weight blended with a hierarchy weight.
A linear program over fractional improvements, stated and not solved.
A mean absolute percentage error between the evaluation and a system-dynamics simulation.

verification.summary: The judgement matrix must pass a consistency ratio below 0.1, though no ratio is computed.
The good level returns an error of 7.6 percent, set against a ten percent line.
The error stays under five percent as the relative size of the seaport changes.

results_trace.summary: The rescaled maturity is 0.8173, inside the Good band.
The percentage error at the good level is 7.6 percent.
The mined standard: people at level four, technology at level three or four, process at level four.
The size test keeps every error below five percent.

writing_logic.summary: Each task is compressed into a first-then-finally sequence ending on a number.
The indicator section rejects the bigger-the-better rule before choosing.
The weaknesses say what the evidence allows and what it rules out.

language_observations.summary: With the development of technology, it is more and more important to establish a suitable system.
The systematic index system is definitely not the bigger the better.
There is still room for improvement to a certain extent.
Which is high precision, verifying the validity and stability of the model.
Due to space limitations, our work can only do this for the time being.
Which proves that. It also confirms. Only slightly lacking in. Mutual benefit and win-win.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 6 draws the indicator weights as horizontal bars, but the values repeat inside groups and cannot sum to one.
Figure 7 is a color bar from zero to one with five named bands and the marker inside Good.
Figure 10 is a radar chart of the good level against the excellent level across eight grouped indicators.
Figure 14 plots the error against seaport size and is said to stay below five percent.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A judge can read the whole result off one color bar: the number, the band, and the distance to the top band.
The radar chart is the only place the investment advice is grounded, since the linear program is never solved.

weaknesses.summary: The entropy formula uses a frequency f_ij that is never defined.
The bar-chart weights repeat within groups and cannot be the combined weights.
The budget constraint weights cost by the indicator score, and the index constraint adds symbols that are not variables.
The rule table keeps rules whose support and confidence fall below the stated thresholds, and the prose quotes numbers the table does not print.
The paper concedes it can only compare simulation with evaluation and cannot test on real company data.

independent_extensions.summary: Fixing the mix of an objective and a subjective weight by equating their gap to the gap between the two weight vectors would transfer to any evaluation that blends two weighting methods.

unresolved_questions: Why does equation (3) leave f_ij undefined?
Why does equation (14) weight the cost by the indicator score rather than by its weight?
Why does equation (16) constrain the index symbols rather than the indicator counts?
Why do the Figure 6 weights repeat inside groups and fail to sum to one?
Why does Table 4 keep rules below the stated support and confidence thresholds?
Why does the prose quote 85.71 percent where the table prints 85.17 percent?
Why does the sum in equation (17) run over i while the terms use t?
What are the system-dynamics equations, the software, and the parameter values?
